QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_73

question.text: An anchor LP asks Mr. Devendra to CAP operating expenses at 25 bps of commitments vs typical 40 bps. GP's best response:

answer.text: Offer 30 bps with a carve-out for extraordinary items (major litigation/regulatory) subject to LPAC approval
Agree only if LP waives MFN rights
Agree at 25 bps and absorb overruns from mgmt fee

explanation.text: The Logic: A balanced counter: 30 bps cap (mid-point concession) with carve-out for genuinely extraordinary items, subject to LPAC approval — protects both GP sustainability and LP predictability. The Trap: Option A loses the anchor. Option C is aggressive and risks reputation. Option D absorbs unquantifiable risk into mgmt fee. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B for fee negotiation; XIX-C for fund ops. Manager's Pro-Tip: Any expense cap tighter than industry norm (40-50 bps per Ch 9.1) should include the extraordinary-items carve-out. Otherwise you absorb regulatory fines or major litigation from GP's own pocket — a dangerous precedent.
